abstract:
Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? Our work begins with a simple observation: content producers do not act in isolation. Instead, they compete with one another (e.g., for customers or attention). We explore the impact competition has on both content diversity and overall social welfare when producers use generative AI. Through a formal game-theoretic model, we show that competitive markets select for diverse AI models, mitigating monoculture. We further show that a generative AI model that performs well in isolation (i.e., according to a benchmark) may fail to provide value in a competitive market. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating generative AI models across the breadth of their output distributions, particularly when they will be deployed in competitive environments. We validate our theoretical results with a series of experiments involving generative text and image models. Overall, our results suggest that homogenization due to generative AI is unlikely to persist under strong competition.
                  This paper was accepted by Itai Ashlagi, market design, platform, and demand analytics.
                  Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02761 .

ob.tldr: 研究生成式AI市场中竞争对内容多样性的影响。通过博弈论模型与文本/图像生成实验发现，竞争性市场会筛选出差异化的AI模型，缓解内容同质化；在基准测试中表现优异的模型未必在竞争环境中创造价值，强调应从输出分布全貌评估生成式AI。

title: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI
